configuration_review.evidence: Source-level expected path removal only. CI must collect generated AND installed configuration.h defines, structured configdata disabled map, runtime disabled listings, negative CMS/QUIC/SIV registration checks, positive native group/signature/AES-GCM capability, static linkage and real mTLS. No successful Actions evidence reviewed; affected_ranges remain blocking. The 20261117 notice adds one QUIC path plus two non-QUIC paths, so the candidate reduction cannot clear the complete notice. Official 4.1.1 tag API returned 404 on 2026-11-17 and the official source table still lists 4.1.0; no 4.1.1 pin or checksum is available.

applicability.CVE-2026-88822: 4.1.0 affected upstream: QUIC automated peer detection leaks stack data. For the five exact configurations above, no-quic is expected to exclude the QUIC implementation (OPENSSL_NO_QUIC), not patch it. Runtime/header/linkage and mTLS evidence pending; CI still blocks. Remaining 3.6.5 is unsupported/unanalysed.
applicability.CVE-2026-95691: 4.1.0 affected upstream: retransmitted QUIC CRYPTO client UAF. Same no-quic removal expectation for the five exact configurations; no whole-program or produced-binary proof yet. CI still blocks.
applicability.CVE-2026-88823: 4.1.0 affected upstream: AES-GCM-SIV fragmented/zero-length AAD authentication error. no-siv controls both SIV and GCM-SIV implementation sources and default-provider registration. Require OPENSSL_NO_SIV plus no AES-*-SIV/AES-*-GCM-SIV runtime registration; ordinary AES-GCM retained. Evidence pending; CI still blocks.
applicability.CVE-2026-95692: 4.1.0 affected upstream: AES-GCM-SIV short/long IV handling. Same no-siv removal expectation, not an AES-GCM TLS vulnerability or a patch. Evidence pending; CI still blocks.
applicability.CVE-2026-107496: CMS_encrypt/CMS_encrypt_ex with attacker-controlled EC order=1 recipient. Advisory limits 4.x exposure to enable-ec_explicit_curves; these configurations do not enable it and additionally use no-cms. Require OPENSSL_NO_CMS and OPENSSL_NO_EC_EXPLICIT_CURVES and absent CMS CLI registration. TLS/QUIC do not use the CMS path, but that fact alone is not a waiver. Evidence pending; CI still blocks.
applicability.CVE-2026-35190: 20261117: 4.1.0 is affected. TLS 1.3 server key-share processing can read beyond a fixed group list only when SSL_CTX_set_cert_flags() sets SSL_CERT_FLAG_SUITEB_128_LOS. The advisory says default configurations and stock s_server -suiteB_128 do not reach it. no-quic/no-cms/no-siv does not remove this TLS path; absence of a project call is not a whole-program waiver. 4.1.1 is not released as of this review, so CI blocks.
applicability.CVE-2026-107493: 20261117: 4.1.0 is affected. PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex() and related functions can leave freed entries when appending to a caller-supplied stack fails. The advisory says OpenSSL's own CA-loading callers pass NULL; only applications supplying an existing stack and using it after failure are affected. no-quic/no-cms/no-siv does not remove this parser path and no call-graph waiver is claimed. 4.1.1 is not released as of this review, so CI blocks.
applicability.CVE-2026-124709: 20261117: 4.1.0 is affected. A QUIC server can retain rejected stream state without bound. no-quic is expected to remove this implementation for the five exact configurations, subject to the same generated-header/configdata/static-symbol evidence as the earlier QUIC CVEs. That candidate path removal neither patches 4.1.0 nor addresses the two other 20261117 findings; CI still blocks.

status: 20261110 and 20261117 notices reviewed. OpenSSL 4.1.1 was not published at query time: the official GitHub tag API returned 404 and the official download table still listed 4.1.0, so no fixed-version migration or SHA-256 can honestly be added. The 4.1.0 reduced builds remain unapproved migration candidates, NOT a CVE waiver. All eight 4.1.0 findings through 20261117 remain encoded in affected_ranges and blocking; no-quic can only address the three QUIC paths as a build-removal candidate, while the Suite B TLS and PEM_X509_INFO paths require separate review or an actually released fixed version. New notices require renewed review; no advisory is suppressed.
